capabilities.semantic_boundary: Joins a circle you were invited to. Once accepted you start sharing your location with, and seeing shares from, that circle's members. This only works on an invitation already pending for you; if you have a code instead, use open_join_circle. A bare 'accept' or 'approve' while a circle invite is the thing in view means this, not approve_request.

capabilities.intent: Add people to share location with
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Opens Connect, where you find and connect with people. Location can only be shared with a connection or a circle member, so this is the way out of an empty people list.
Adds one person to the list who are alerted and receive your live location if you trigger an SOS. Only people who have finished Location setup can be added.

Invites one or more of your connections to join a circle -- multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. They are not in the circle until they accept, so this sends an invitation rather than adding them outright. Only people already connected to you can be invited.

Approves the named people's pending requests to see your location, starting a share for each -- multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only acts on requests already waiting; it never invites someone new. A bare 'approve' or 'accept' with no name and no circle invite in view means this; if a circle invite is what's actually pending, call accept_circle_invite instead.

capabilities.intent: Change how long a share lasts
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Changes how much longer the named person can see your live location, without stopping and restarting the share. It only acts on a share already active with them.
Delegates live-location status and client-side location directives to the Location specialist under One.

Ends your current Nearby Check-In presence, so you stop showing up to people nearby. It does not affect any other kind of location share. Works from any screen -- you do not need to be on the Check-In or Map screens to check out.

Finishes a nearby check-in already started by nearby_check_in: matches the named place against the nearby candidates it returned and, once a duration is given, checks in immediately. Only works after nearby_check_in has listed candidates in this conversation; if the named place does not match any of them, it stops and Check-In stays open for the person to search manually instead of guessing.

Creates a circle with the name the person says, without opening the create-circle screen. If no name was said, asks for one first. A new circle starts empty; people join only after they accept an invitation.

Declines a pending invitation to join a circle. Nothing is shared and the invitation is closed; you can be invited again later. A bare 'decline' while a circle invite is the thing in view means this, not decline_request.

Declines the named people's pending requests to see your location -- multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only acts on requests already waiting and does not stop any share already in place with them. A bare 'decline' with no name and no circle invite in view means this; if a circle invite is what's actually pending, call decline_circle_invite instead.
Permanently deletes a circle you own. Every member loses the access and sharing that circle provided; this cannot be undone. Only the circle's owner can delete it.
Permanently removes a saved place from your list. It does not affect any active or past shares of your location; it only forgets the saved point itself.
Checks your phone contacts against Hushh accounts and shows which of them are already here. Phone numbers are hashed on your device; your contact list is never stored.

Removes you from a circle you belong to, so you stop sharing your location with it and stop seeing its members' shares. The circle itself and its other members are untouched. Its owner cannot leave -- they must delete it or hand off ownership first.

Starts checking in to a nearby place: opens Check-In if not already there, then looks up the places closest to you right now. If the place is already named in the same turn and it matches one of the nearby results, confirm_nearby_check_in should be called next to finish. Otherwise it lists the nearby options for the person to choose from; if nothing plausible is nearby, Check-In stays open for the person to search manually.

capabilities.intent: Choose how to handle a place during Location setup
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Applies only while Location setup is waiting for a place choice. It can use Home or Work, request a custom label, or skip saving the optional place. The choice is completed only after the approved interaction finishes; it never declares the entire setup complete.

Opens the list of shares that are live right now, so you can see what other people can currently see. A bare 'stop sharing' with no name attached stops your own device broadcasting instead (see pause_updates) -- use this to just look, or when a person IS already named (e.g. 'stop sharing with Alice'), call stop_share directly.

Opens the request composer, where you ask another person to share location with you. If the person is already named in the same request (e.g. 'ask Alice where she is'), call select_ask_recipient directly instead -- it navigates here and selects them in one step.
Opens check-in, where you send a one-off note of where you are to people you choose.
Opens the create-circle screen, where you name a new circle of people to share location with as a group.
Opens the invite screen, where you invite someone who is not on Hushh yet to share location with you.

Opens the join-circle screen, where you enter an invite code to join someone else's circle. Use this only when you have a code to type in; if you already have a pending circle invitation waiting for you, call accept_circle_invite directly instead -- no code needed.
Opens the Links tab of Location, which lists temporary sharing links you have created.
Opens the full-screen map of the people sharing location with you.
Opens the requests waiting on your decision, where you approve or decline people asking to see your location.
Opens the Overview tab of Location, which shows current sharing status and the quick actions.
Opens the People tab of Location, which lists the people and circles you share with.
Opens the Location settings screen, which holds the privacy and precision controls for location sharing.

Opens the share composer, where you pick who to share your location with and for how long. Nothing is shared until you send it. If the person to share with is already named in the same request (e.g. 'share my location with Alice'), call select_share_recipient directly instead -- it navigates here and selects them in one step. If the composer is already open with people already picked and the person just says 'share my location' again to finish, that means send it now -- call share_selected instead, not this.
Opens the list of people who are currently sharing location with you.

Opens the Save My Soul contacts screen, where you choose who is alerted when you raise an SOS. SMS is short for Save My Soul; no text message is sent -- contacts get a push notification, an email fallback, and a live location share.

Opens the emergency SOS screen, where an alert with your location can be sent to your emergency contacts. Opening it does not send anything. Say this only when the person explicitly asks to look at the screen or manage contacts, not for a bare or ambiguous emergency phrase like 'help' or 'save me' -- those go to sos_default instead, which respects the person's own SOS default. To send a real alert immediately, use trigger_sos.
Opens the temporary link screen, where you create a link that shows your location for a limited time to anyone who opens it.

Stops this device sending new location updates and takes you off nearby presence. This is what a bare 'stop sharing' with no name attached means -- the safe, decisive reading of an urgent request. People you have already granted keep their grant, but it stops moving until you resume. This affects your device for everyone at once; to end a share with just one person while staying visible to everyone else, use stop_share instead.
Reloads location sharing state so shares, requests and grants are current.
Removes one person from the list who are alerted and receive your live location if you trigger an SOS.
Removes one person from a circle, so they stop receiving your location through it. The circle itself and its other members are left untouched.
Changes a circle's name. It only renames the circle; its members, invitations, and shares through it are untouched.
Turns location updates back on for this device and refreshes your live position. This makes you visible again to everyone you have an active grant with, so it asks before it runs.

capabilities.intent: Save your current location as a place
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Saves where you are right now as a named place -- home, work, or a custom name. Home and work replace any earlier place saved under that same category; a custom name is added alongside your existing places.

capabilities.intent: Pick someone to ask for location
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Finds the person or people you named among your connections and selects them in the request composer, so you can see who is picked before anything is sent. Multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only selects: sending the request is still a separate, confirmed step. Works from any screen: it navigates to this composer itself, so open_ask does not need to be called first when a name is already given.

Finds the person or people you named among your connections and selects them in the share composer, so you can see who is picked before anything is sent. Multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only selects: starting the share is still a separate, confirmed step. Works from any screen: it navigates to this composer itself, so open_share does not need to be called first when a name is already given.

capabilities.intent: Send the check-in you have open
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Sends the check-in currently on screen to the people already selected there, using its already-set duration and message. It only works while the Check-In screen is open; it does not open Check-In or change who or how long it targets.

Sends a request to see location. If one or more people are named in the same turn (e.g. 'ask Alice and Bob for location'), it resolves and sends to them directly -- no need to select first. Otherwise it sends to whoever is already picked in the request composer, and never chooses who: if nobody is selected it stops and asks you to pick someone first.

capabilities.intent: Turn automatic approval of location requests on or off
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Controls whether incoming location requests are approved without asking the person each time. Applies only to requests that arrive after it is switched on; requests already waiting still need an explicit answer.

capabilities.intent: Share with the people I picked
capabilities.semantic_boundary: Shares your live location with the people already selected in the share composer, for the length of time you say. If one or more people are named in the same turn (e.g. 'share my location with Alice and Bob for 2 hours'), it resolves and shares with them directly -- no need to select first. Otherwise it shares with whoever is already picked in the share composer, and never chooses who: if nobody is selected it stops and asks you to pick someone first. This is what 'share my location' means once the composer is already open with people picked -- open_share is only for starting from cold.

Handles a bare or ambiguous emergency phrase -- 'save me', 'sos', 'help', 'emergency', 'turn on sos' -- by doing whatever the person's own SOS default says: either opening the SOS screen so they can decide, or going straight to the send-alert confirm card. Change the default in Voice Settings. Never use this for an explicit 'open the SOS screen' (use open_sos) or an explicit 'send an SOS' (use trigger_sos) -- those always do exactly what they say, regardless of this default.

Stops active shares with the named people immediately, so your location no longer updates for them -- multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only ends the shares you named; every other active share is untouched. It does not touch your device's own broadcasting -- to stop sharing with everyone at once, use pause_updates instead.
Ends an SOS that is currently running and revokes every location share it created. It does not tell anyone you are safe.

Sends an emergency alert to your ready emergency contacts right now, sharing your live location with them and emailing anyone a push notification could not reach. It does not call emergency services. This is a real, immediate alert, not the SOS screen -- to just look at the screen or manage contacts without alerting anyone, use open_sos.
Requires a real operating system result and cannot be simulated.
Requests final verification after the Location onboarding runtime has settled permission, position, place or explicit skip, and personal Circle provisioning.

Pauses the active Location onboarding run and returns to setup without recording Location as complete.

Stops this device sending new location updates and takes you off nearby presence. This is what a bare 'stop sharing' with no name attached means -- the safe, decisive reading of an urgent request. People you have already granted keep their grant, but it stops moving until you resume. This affects your device for everyone at once; to end a share with just one person while staying visible to everyone else, use stop_share instead.
Reloads location sharing state so shares, requests and grants are current.
Removes one person from the list who are alerted and receive your live location if you trigger an SOS.
Removes one person from a circle, so they stop receiving your location through it. The circle itself and its other members are left untouched.
Changes a circle's name. It only renames the circle; its members, invitations, and shares through it are untouched.
Turns location updates back on for this device and refreshes your live position. This makes you visible again to everyone you have an active grant with, so it asks before it runs.

capability_cards.intent: Save your current location as a place
capability_cards.semantic_boundary: Saves where you are right now as a named place -- home, work, or a custom name. Home and work replace any earlier place saved under that same category; a custom name is added alongside your existing places.

capability_cards.intent: Pick someone to ask for location
capability_cards.semantic_boundary: Finds the person or people you named among your connections and selects them in the request composer, so you can see who is picked before anything is sent. Multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only selects: sending the request is still a separate, confirmed step. Works from any screen: it navigates to this composer itself, so open_ask does not need to be called first when a name is already given.

Finds the person or people you named among your connections and selects them in the share composer, so you can see who is picked before anything is sent. Multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only selects: starting the share is still a separate, confirmed step. Works from any screen: it navigates to this composer itself, so open_share does not need to be called first when a name is already given.

capability_cards.intent: Send the check-in you have open
capability_cards.semantic_boundary: Sends the check-in currently on screen to the people already selected there, using its already-set duration and message. It only works while the Check-In screen is open; it does not open Check-In or change who or how long it targets.

Sends a request to see location. If one or more people are named in the same turn (e.g. 'ask Alice and Bob for location'), it resolves and sends to them directly -- no need to select first. Otherwise it sends to whoever is already picked in the request composer, and never chooses who: if nobody is selected it stops and asks you to pick someone first.

capability_cards.intent: Turn automatic approval of location requests on or off
capability_cards.semantic_boundary: Controls whether incoming location requests are approved without asking the person each time. Applies only to requests that arrive after it is switched on; requests already waiting still need an explicit answer.

capability_cards.intent: Share with the people I picked
capability_cards.semantic_boundary: Shares your live location with the people already selected in the share composer, for the length of time you say. If one or more people are named in the same turn (e.g. 'share my location with Alice and Bob for 2 hours'), it resolves and shares with them directly -- no need to select first. Otherwise it shares with whoever is already picked in the share composer, and never chooses who: if nobody is selected it stops and asks you to pick someone first. This is what 'share my location' means once the composer is already open with people picked -- open_share is only for starting from cold.

Handles a bare or ambiguous emergency phrase -- 'save me', 'sos', 'help', 'emergency', 'turn on sos' -- by doing whatever the person's own SOS default says: either opening the SOS screen so they can decide, or going straight to the send-alert confirm card. Change the default in Voice Settings. Never use this for an explicit 'open the SOS screen' (use open_sos) or an explicit 'send an SOS' (use trigger_sos) -- those always do exactly what they say, regardless of this default.

Stops active shares with the named people immediately, so your location no longer updates for them -- multiple people can be named in one turn, e.g. 'Alice and Bob'. It only ends the shares you named; every other active share is untouched. It does not touch your device's own broadcasting -- to stop sharing with everyone at once, use pause_updates instead.
Ends an SOS that is currently running and revokes every location share it created. It does not tell anyone you are safe.

Sends an emergency alert to your ready emergency contacts right now, sharing your live location with them and emailing anyone a push notification could not reach. It does not call emergency services. Use this only when the person explicitly says to send, trigger, or call for help right now -- for a bare or ambiguous emergency phrase like 'help' or 'save me', use sos_default instead, which respects the person's own SOS default rather than assuming they meant send. This is a real, immediate alert, not the SOS screen -- to just look at the screen or manage contacts without alerting anyone, use open_sos.
